title: The Cloud Baker

before.title: The Cloud Baker
before.text: Every morning, Sami makes bread in a tower. He uses flour, water, and one piece of cloud. The bread stays soft for seven days. One windy morning, all the clouds move away. Sami cannot finish his work. He ties white cloth to the tower. Birds see it and carry small pieces of cloud to him. Sami thanks them with warm bread.

after.title: The Cloud Baker
after.text: Every morning, Sami makes bread in a tower. He uses flour, water, and one piece of cloud. The bread stays soft for seven days. One windy morning, all the clouds move away. Sami cannot finish his work. He ties white cloth to the tower. Birds see it and carry small pieces of cloud to him. Sami thanks them with warm bread.

reason: A fantasy baker uses cloud as an ingredient, runs out when the wind moves the clouds, and gets help from birds. The tower, bread and birds have clear referents. The seven-day softness and cloud-carrying belong to an openly magical story, not baking advice.

title: A Quiet Table for Grandfather

before.title: A Quiet Table for Grandfather
before.text: Maya has dinner with her grandfather. He cannot hear well when many people talk at once. Maya first puts him near the kitchen, but the dishes are loud. She moves a small table away from the noise. Everyone takes turns sitting with him. Now he can hear their stories, and the whole family can enjoy the meal together.

after.title: A Quiet Table for Grandfather
after.text: Maya has dinner with her grandfather. He finds it hard to hear when many people talk at once. At first, they sit near the kitchen, but the dishes are loud. Maya asks if they can move to a small table away from the noise. Her grandfather agrees. Family members take turns sitting with him and telling stories. He can now hear them better, and everyone enjoys the meal.

reason: Replaces Maya putting her grandfather somewhere with a request and his agreement. Kitchen noise, move and conversation follow in order. Better is a bounded result for this imagined family, not a universal hearing intervention.

title: Water Marks in the School Hall

before.title: Water Marks in the School Hall
before.text: Wet footprints cross the school hall, then stop at a wall. A girl follows them after class. There is no door or window nearby. She looks up and sees drops on a pipe. The wet shoes of a school worker made the first marks. Then he went up some high steps to fix the pipe. The last marks are on those steps.

after.title: Water Marks in the School Hall
after.text: Wet footprints cross the school hall and stop at a wall. A girl follows them after class. There is no door nearby. She looks up and sees a ladder by the wall. Water drips from a pipe above it. A school worker walked there in wet shoes, then climbed the ladder to fix the pipe. The girl now knows why the footprints stopped.

reason: The original footprints stopped at a wall but its final marks were on high steps, leaving the route contradictory. A ladder beside the wall explains where the worker went and why the floor marks stop. The mystery remains a short coherent Level 2 fiction.

title: Omar Makes a Bus Map

before.title: Omar and the Talking Map
before.text: Omar drives a bus in a busy town. New riders often miss their stops because the street signs are small. He records short stop names in three languages and asks a student to add them to a simple map. Riders can press a button to hear the next stop. Omar did not build a new bus. He made the old one easier to use.

after.title: Omar Makes a Bus Map
after.text: Omar is a fictional bus driver. New riders sometimes miss their stops because the street signs are small. Omar makes a map with stop names in three languages. He puts it near the front of his bus. He also calls out each stop. A rider points to the map and asks about the library stop. Omar tells her when to get off. He did not build a new bus; he made the route easier for this rider to follow.

reason: A map that talks through a button was asserted without explaining how the bus was changed. A printed map and spoken stops give the rider a clear, plausible way to find the stop. The text identifies Omar as invented.

title: The Note in the Empty Jar

before.title: The Note in the Empty Jar
before.text: A note appears inside an empty glass jar at the cafe. It says, “Look under the red seat.” Bo checks every red chair but finds nothing. Then he sees a child holding a red toy bus. Under its seat is a tiny paper heart. The note was part of a birthday game.

after.title: The Note in the Empty Jar
after.text: Bo sees a note inside a glass jar that was empty yesterday. It says, “Look under the red seat.” He checks every red chair in the cafe but finds nothing. Then a child shows him a toy bus with a red seat. Under that seat is a tiny paper heart. The child smiles. The note was part of a birthday game.

reason: The jar is only said to have been empty yesterday, removing the contradiction of a note in an empty jar. The toy bus actually has a red seat, so the clue resolves without changing the words on the note.

title: Dani Opens a Tool Box

before.text: Dani repairs chairs and tables. Many neighbors throw things away because they have no tools. Dani puts simple tools in a box at the library. People may borrow them with a card. On Saturdays, Dani shows how to use each tool safely. Soon, broken chairs begin to return to use.

after.title: Dani Opens a Tool Box

One neighbor fixes a chair and brings it back to show Dani.
